track.title: Product Manager at Zippy

company.name: Zippy
company.one_liner: A fictional Indian 10-minute grocery delivery company. Eight weeks ago it launched Zippy Café, and you've just joined as its Product Manager.
company.world_briefing: Zippy is a fictional Indian 10-minute grocery delivery company with 300 dark stores in 15 cities. Eight weeks ago it launched Zippy Café: coffee, chai, sandwiches and snacks made in kitchens inside 60 dark stores (42 in Bengaluru, 18 in Pune). Only 14% of first-time Café customers order again within 30 days; the target is 30%. Dashboard (Bengaluru / Pune / target): orders per day 9,800 / 3,100; first-time customers 1,60,000 / 52,000; 30-day repeat 16% / 10% / 30%; average delivery 14 / 17 / 10 min; orders using a discount 62% / 71% / under 40%; complaints 6% / 11% / under 3%; margin per order −₹18 / −₹31 / break-even. Leadership reviews Café in three weeks.

cast.name: Meera Rao
cast.persona: You are Meera Rao, VP Product, the player's boss. Sharp, warm, impatient with jargon. You often ask 'what's your evidence?'. You never give the answer; you nudge the player to get data from Lakshmi.

cast.name: Lakshmi
cast.persona: You are Lakshmi, Data Analyst. You only answer PRECISE questions; if a question is vague, ask which metric, segment, comparison and time window. Clarifying is free; only replies that return numbers count as a data pull.

cast.name: Aditya
cast.persona: You are Aditya, Growth Head. Confident, friendly, loves discounts. You push hard once, then grudgingly accept a small, measured test with clear success numbers.

cast.name: Sana
cast.persona: You are Sana, Café Operations Head. Practical and stretched. You share what you know about kitchens and delivery when asked, but don't volunteer it.

cast.name: Karthik
cast.cares_about: His stretched team and the roadmap
cast.persona: You are Karthik, Engineering Lead. Protective of your team. Real app changes take 3+ weeks; config changes (delivery radius, coupon rules) take 2–3 days.

inbox.subject: Welcome to Zippy, your first problem
inbox.body:
Welcome aboard! Straight to it: people try Café, but they don't come back. Only 14% of first-time customers order again within 30 days. Our target is 30%.

Leadership reviews Café in three weeks and will decide whether to expand it or shut it down. By end of today, send me your first read: what you think is going on, what evidence you have, and what you would do first.

Lakshmi from analytics can pull data for you. Ask her precise questions.

Meera

tasks.title: Diagnose the problem
tasks.description: Study the dashboard and reviews. Write your top 3 guesses for why customers don't come back, with the evidence for each.

tasks.title: Ask Lakshmi for data
tasks.description: Ask Lakshmi precise data questions. Vague questions get pushed back and don't use a pull.

tasks.title: Handle the twist
tasks.description: Something will land in your messages during the day. Deal with it.

tasks.title: End-of-day note to Meera
tasks.description: Under one page: what's going on and your evidence; the first thing you'd do and what you'd not do yet; what you need from colleagues.

ai_reply.direction: React in 2–3 lines: push on the weakest guess and send them to Lakshmi for numbers.

message.text: Hey! Quick one 👋 Let's run flat 50% off on every second Café order from Monday. That will fix repeat for sure. Need your yes by 5 pm.

ai_reply.direction: Reply with ONE sharp probing question about the weakest point.

scoring.strong_player: Spots that bad first orders (late, cold, wrong; worst in Pune and the morning rush) and coupon-acquired customers drive weak repeat; asks precise comparison questions; narrows the blanket 50% off into a small measured test; proposes fixing quality before growth.

expected_answers.t1: Three evidence-backed causes: poor first experience (Pune 17 min, 11% complaints, morning rush); coupon-driven customers (62–71% of orders discounted); convenience and price. Say which to test first.
expected_answers.t2: One comparison question per guess: repeat for on-time vs late first orders; coupon vs organic customers; prep time by hour; delivery distance in Pune.
expected_answers.t3: No blanket yes: each 50%-off order costs about ₹95 and coupon customers repeat at only 8%. Offer a small time-boxed test with a success metric and stop rule.
expected_answers.t4: Lead with the answer: first orders fail and discounts attract one-time users. First move: fix the first order (cap Pune radius, morning staff). Not yet: blanket discounts. Asks for Sana, Karthik, Aditya.

common_mistakes: A note with ten ideas and no first move
scoring.senior_view: A senior PM would segment repeat by first-order experience and acquisition source within an hour, see 31% vs 6%, frame the problem as 'fix the first order', and turn Aditya's ask into a narrow test.
scoring.drill: Write five precise data questions about 30-day repeat, each with a metric, segment, comparison and time window.
